First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+16}}\cdot ⟨t,4⟩) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+16}})\cdot ⟨t,4⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+16}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(⟨t,4⟩) \\  & =-\frac{t}{({t}^{2}+16)\sqrt{{t}^{2}+16}}\cdot ⟨t,4⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+16}}\cdot ⟨1,0⟩ \\  \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{0}{({0}^{2}+16)\sqrt{{0}^{2}+16}}\cdot ⟨0,4⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{0}^{2}+16}}\cdot ⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

  

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{1}{4}‖⟨1,0⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(0)$ and obtain the principal normal vector to the curve at the point where $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{4}⟨1,0⟩}{(\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =⟨1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\cdot N(0) & =\frac{1}{4}⟨0,4⟩\cdot ⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(0+0) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the magnitude of T′(0):

‖T′(0)‖=14‖⟨1,0⟩‖=1412+02=14

Finally, we normalize T′(0) and obtain the principal normal vector to the curve at the point where t=0:

N(0)=T′(0)‖T′(0)‖=14⟨1,0⟩(14)=⟨1,0⟩

Note that when we find the scalar product of T and N at the point where t=0, we get

T(0)⋅N(0)=14⟨0,4⟩⋅⟨1,0⟩=14(0+0)=0.✓
